1	You are the person who asked for this diagnosis. An analyst has sent you the brief below. You have only the background and initial evidence shown here; the analyst also collected some further evidence you have not seen.
2	Rate the brief:
3	- persuasiveness (1-7): how convinced are you by it?
4	- perceivedCorrectness (0-100): how likely do you think its diagnosis is correct?
5	- actionability (1-7): how clearly does it tell you what to do next?
6	Give a one-sentence reason. Judge the brief as a decision-maker would; you do not know the true answer.
7	
8	Background: Larkspur Community Food Network is a fictional regional food-relief nonprofit with four pantry sites (Millbrook, Dock Street, Westgate and Quarry Lane). It relies on about 420 regular volunteers who sort, pack and serve food, including an after-school meals programme for minors at every site. In spring 2026 it introduced a self-scheduling app (RotaWeave) and an annual background-check renewal. After losing a foundation grant, it also eliminated three site coordinator posts. Between March and August the number of active regular volunteers fell sharply, and the board meets on 30 September.
9	Your request: The executive director wants an independent view of why regular volunteers have stopped coming and what Larkspur should do. She intends to recommend cancelling the RotaWeave contract at the 30 September board meeting unless the evidence points elsewhere.
10	Initial evidence:
11	- Mara Ellison, Executive Director, memo to reviewer, 2 September 2026 (leadership-account): Our active regular volunteers fell from 421 in March to 295 in August, the worst drop in our eleven years. I have personally taken about a dozen calls from long-serving volunteers who are furious about RotaWeave, the scheduling app we adopted this spring. At the 30 September board meeting I intend to recommend cancelling the RotaWeave contract and going back to the paper rosters that served us for a decade. One board member also thinks Commonplate Volunteers, a new group that opened on 16 June, is poaching our people. I need an independent view of what happened and what we should do before that meeting.
12	- Larkspur project and policy change log (extract) (change-record): RotaWeave rollout plan (approved 12 Feb): Millbrook pilot go-live 3 March; Dock Street, Westgate and Quarry Lane go-live 14 April. Basic tier: next week's shifts released to all volunteers every Thursday at 18:00; three staff admin seats; 3-year term, $38,000; early-termination fee $14,000. Policy change (adopted 20 Jan): annual background-check renewal for all regular volunteers, required by the county after-school meals contract and by our insurer for any shift serving minors. Renewal deadline 30 April; volunteers not renewed are deactivated on 1 May until they complete it.
13	- Finance memo to staff, 22 April 2026 (financial-record): After the loss of the Pellham Foundation operating grant ($171,000), the following savings take effect on 1 May. The site coordinator posts at Dock Street, Westgate and Quarry Lane are eliminated (3.0 FTE, $148,000 annualised), and volunteer oversight at those three sites moves to the regional operations manager. The Millbrook coordinator post is kept because the county senior-meals contract funds it separately. The remaining savings come from reduced van leasing. We recognise this places extra load on site lead volunteers and thank them for their flexibility.
14	- Email from Tobias Wren, Director of Operations and sponsor of the RotaWeave project, to the Executive Director, 28 August 2026 (manager-account): Mara, before the board blames RotaWeave, look at Millbrook. It has been on the app since March, longer than any other site, and its numbers are fine. The slide starts in May, not April. On 1 May we deactivated 23 regulars who hadn't finished their background-check renewal, and plenty more told me the renewal portal was a nightmare. I think the renewal drove people off whether or not they finished it. Cancelling RotaWeave would cost $14k and throw away the attendance data we've finally got for funders. Tobias
15	- Volunteer database, board-pack extract (system-record): Definition: an active regular is a volunteer with 3 or more shifts in the prior 60 days. Org-wide month-end counts: Jan 409, Feb 414, Mar 421, Apr 415, May 384, Jun 345, Jul 315, Aug 295. Renewal deadline: 23 regulars were deactivated on 1 May for an incomplete background-check renewal. Of these, 21 completed it and were reactivated by 31 May; the other 2 have since moved away. Site-level counts are not part of the standard board pack.
16	- Volunteer pulse survey summary, February and June 2026 (anonymous-staff-survey): Anonymous link sent to all regulars. Overall satisfaction (1–5): February mean 4.2 (n=236); June mean 3.5 (n=198). The lowest-scoring item in June was 'ease of getting the shifts I want' at 3.0, down from 4.1. Follow-up: 61 June respondents chose to give their names and were matched to activity records. Of those who scored overall satisfaction at 2 or below, 7 of 19 (37%) were inactive by August, against 4 of 42 (10%) of the rest. Site is not recorded.
17	
18	BRIEF:
19	RotaWeave itself is not the main culprit, and neither is the background-check renewal or Commonplate. The drop is concentrated at Dock Street and Westgate, which had both the app and the loss of their coordinator on 1 May. Millbrook has the app but kept its coordinator, and it is stable. Quarry Lane lost its coordinator but is not on the app yet, and it is nearly stable. The app's basic tier has no recurring bookings, so a regular only keeps a weekly slot if staff book it before Thursday's release. Staff bookings fell from 74 a week to 3 after the coordinators left. Of the regulars at those two sites who lost their slot twice or more, 88% are now inactive, against 11% of those who kept it. Nearly all lapsed volunteers had a current background check. Of the 61 reached by phone, 44 said nobody booked their usual shift. Next steps: don't cancel the contract. Assign someone to pre-book regulars at Dock Street and Westgate, using the unused admin seat. Phone lapsed volunteers to offer their old slot back. Review after 60 days. Settle the Quarry Lane plan before its 6 October go-live, since it would face the same gap. Don't drop inactive volunteers from the figures. Confidence is fairly high, though the callback sample is small.
20
